title: Retain-Neutral Surrogates for Min-Max Unlearning
claim: Forget and retain gradients are strongly coupled in common settings, so the standard perturbation raises retain loss while an orthogonal one avoids it.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: bar chart, scatter plot, geometric vector diagram
description: Three panels, labeled (a) Coupling diagnosis, (b) Retain-orthogonal surrogate, (c) Retain-neutral amplification. Panel (a) is a bar chart of cos θ(w) across datasets. Blue bars for class-wise forgetting are low (0.05, 0.19, 0.15). Red bars for 10%-random forgetting are high (0.76, 0.91, 0.88). A purple TOFU bar is 0.92. Dashed lines separate the groups, and value labels sit above the bars. Panel (b) is a density scatter of CIFAR-100 samples, colored from blue to red. It plots the retain-gradient projection against the forget-gradient projection and shows a strong positive correlation. A black arrow δ_std points diagonally up and right. A purple arrow δ_rosu lies along the horizontal line g_r^T δ = 0. Panel (c) is a vector sketch. It shows g_r pointing up in green, g_f tilted in orange, and the angle θ between them. A black δ_std and purple δ_rosu start at w, and a longer dark arrow β δ_rosu continues along the retain-neutral line.
caption: (a) The coupling \(\cos\theta(w)\) between the forget and retain gradients \(g_f(w)\) and \(g_r(w)\) is low in class-wise forgetting and high in random forgetting and TOFU. (b) In a highly coupled setting, \(\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\mathrm{std}}\) moves toward higher forget and retain losses, while \(\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\mathrm{rosu}}\) moves toward higher forget loss on the retain-neutral hyperplane \(g_r(w)^\top\boldsymbol{\delta}=0\). The arrows indicate directions. (c) The same direction \(\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\mathrm{rosu}}\) sets the surrogate point, and its amplification \(\beta\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\mathrm{rosu}}\) is the forgetting step, which stays retain-neutral.
abstract: Machine unlearning aims to make a model forget designated training data while retaining performance on the rest. In min-max unlearning, an inner adversary perturbs the model to maximize the forget loss, and the model is updated to minimize the retain loss at the resulting surrogate point. When the forget and retain gradients are positively coupled, the standard perturbation also moves toward higher retain loss, and the retain step begins by recovering that loss. We propose Retain-Orthogonal Surrogate Unlearning (ROSU), which redefines the adversary to admit only perturbations orthogonal to the retain gradient. The one that raises the forget loss fastest has a closed form, and ROSU uses it to set the surrogate point and amplifies it into the forgetting step. Under positive coupling the ROSU surrogate avoids the retain cost that coupling induces in the standard surrogate, and the difference shrinks as the gradients approach orthogonality. ROSU has the smallest accuracy gap to retraining in every vision setting (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet) and is competitive with the baselines on language benchmarks (TOFU, WMDP). The redefinition helps most under high positive coupling. Code is available at https://github.com/unlearn-ml/machine-unlearning.
